# Points Program

### Overview

The Extended Points Program recognises certain eligible activity and contributions to the Extended ecosystem.

Participation is subject to the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md), applicable eligibility requirements and jurisdictional restrictions.

Points are allocated periodically in accordance with the program parameters, allocation methodology, eligibility requirements and anti-abuse controls described on this page. The program may evolve over time, and its terms, operation or availability may be updated, paused or brought to an end in accordance with the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md).

Weekly points distributions have ended. As of 05.11.2026, all 70,000,000 points out of 70 million total points have been distributed under the program.

The cumulative figure is provided for informational purposes only. It does not affect individual allocations or imply any monetary value, token allocation or future entitlement.

### Qualifying activity

Points may be allocated in connection with:

* qualifying trading activity;
* qualifying liquidity-related activity;
* eligible referral or affiliate activity;
* other activity, contributions or circumstances recognised by Extended as supporting the objectives or operation of the program, such as product testing, bug reporting, structured user feedback; and
* exceptional user-impact events, including operational errors or incidents.

Extended may determine the eligibility, amount and timing of any such allocation in accordance with the applicable program parameters. All allocations will be made within the applicable Points pools.

Where Points are allocated in connection with an operational error or incident, the allocation does not imply that Points have a fixed monetary value and, unless expressly agreed otherwise with the affected user, does not by itself constitute reimbursement or settlement of any financial loss.

Engaging in qualifying activity does not create an entitlement to any particular allocation. Allocations may depend on multiple factors, including the nature, quality, consistency and eligibility of the relevant activity.

Users should not trade, deposit, refer others or increase their activity solely for the purpose of obtaining Points.

Participation in the Vault and in leveraged trading products involves significant risk, including possible total loss. Points are not compensation for taking additional risk and should not be understood as a recommendation or encouragement to trade, deposit or increase activity.

### Allocation methodology

The allocation methodology is intended to recognise genuine eligible activity and contributions.

Extended may apply weightings, eligibility thresholds, exclusions, adjustments and anti-abuse controls. The existence of qualifying activity does not guarantee that Points will be allocated or that similar activities will receive identical allocations.

Detailed elements of the methodology may not be disclosed where disclosure could facilitate manipulation, circumvention or abuse.

Material changes to the program parameters or allocation methodology will be reflected in this documentation. Changes may apply immediately where reasonably required for legal, regulatory, security, operational, anti-abuse or error-correction purposes.

### Eligibility and prohibited conduct

Participation is not available to persons who are ineligible under the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md) or located in a restricted jurisdiction.

Points may be withheld, reduced, cancelled or adjusted where activity is determined to involve, among other things:

* wash trading or artificial volume;
* self-referrals or coordinated referral abuse;
* multiple-account manipulation;
* bots or automated activity used to exploit the program;
* fraud, manipulation or circumvention of program rules;
* activity by an ineligible person or from a restricted jurisdiction; or
* an operational, data or calculation error.

Extended may request information reasonably required to verify eligibility, investigate suspected abuse or correct an allocation.

### Nature of Points

Points:

* are program units and are not freely transferable or tradable by users;
* are not money and have no guaranteed monetary value;
* cannot be purchased, sold, transferred or redeemed by users;
* do not confer ownership, governance, profit-sharing, shareholder or similar rights;
* do not currently represent a token, cryptoasset, security or other financial instrument and do not create a present entitlement to receive tokens.

Extended may, at its discretion and in limited circumstances, migrate, reassign or otherwise adjust Points, including following a verified wallet compromise, operational error or program-integrity issue. Any such action does not create a general right for users to transfer Points.

**Points may be taken into account in connection with a future token distribution or other program benefit. Any such distribution or benefit would be subject to separate terms, eligibility requirements, compliance and anti-abuse checks, and the final applicable program mechanics. No particular allocation methodology, conversion ratio, claim process, distribution date, staking option or token value has been confirmed unless expressly confirmed in separate official documentation.**

### Adjustments and program changes

Extended may correct individual or aggregate allocations where necessary to address an error, abuse, manipulation, ineligibility or another program-integrity issue.

Program parameters, eligibility criteria and allocation methodology may be amended, suspended or discontinued.

Where reasonably practicable, material changes will be reflected on this page. Advance notice may not be provided where an immediate change is reasonably required for legal, regulatory, security, operational, anti-abuse or error-correction purposes.

Any future token distribution and claim process will be governed by separate terms made available at the relevant time. Holding Points does not remove the requirement to satisfy those terms, complete any required eligibility or compliance checks, or submit a valid claim.

### Balances and allocation queries

A user's individual Points balance and distribution history are available at:

<https://app.extended.exchange/points>

Balances and distribution records displayed in the user interface may be corrected where necessary to address an error, abuse, manipulation, ineligibility or other program-integrity issue.

Users who believe that an allocation contains an error may submit a query through the applicable support channel. Submission of a query does not guarantee an adjustment.

### Primary source of information

This page is the primary public source for current information about the Points program.

Discord, X and other public communications are informational only and do not amend or override this documentation or the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md).

This page should be read together with the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md). In the event of any inconsistency between this page and the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md), the [Terms of Use](/extended-resources/legal/terms-of-use.md) prevail.

# About HelloTrade

## Overview

HelloTrade is a self-custody brokerage and trading platform for global markets, running on Monad.

We’re building one place to trade 10,000+ markets onchain – stocks, crypto, commodities, ETFs and FX – with up to 50× leverage, 24/7.

The platform is mobile-first with institutional-grade performance.

## Access

We are already live in closed alpha with a core set of initial markets to stress test the platform.

We are opening access deliberately, onboarding enough traders to put real volume through the system before progressing to beta and later, public launch.

To get early access:

1. Join the waitlist at [hello.trade](https://www.hello.trade/)
2. Follow us on [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/hellotradeapp)\
   (Turn notifications on for invite code drops)

## Architecture

HelloTrade employs a hybrid architecture combining the performance of centralized exchanges with the security of decentralized settlement and custody:

* **Performance:** Extremely performant matching engine with <10ms latency on order cancellations
* **On-Chain Settlement**: Non-custodial settlement where all margin operations and positions are tracked on-chain in smart contracts
* **Multi-Protocol Access**: WebSocket and REST interfaces

This design ensures institutional-grade performance while maintaining the transparency and security guarantees of blockchain-based settlement.

## Markets & Liquidity

### 24/7 Trading

Markets trade continuously, even when underlying assets are closed. The exchange operates in different modes based on market conditions:

* **Normal hours**: Full liquidity with standard pricing mechanisms
* **Scheduled closures**: Weekend and holiday trading with price bands to limit volatility
* **Market halts**: Adaptive response to LULD halts, news events, and regulatory actions
* **Corporate events**: Handling of stock splits, M\&A, earnings, and delisting events

## Risk Management

The platform uses a cross-margin system with a single USDM collateral pool supporting positions across all instruments. Leverage up to 50x is available.

A multi-layer liquidation system protects the exchange and its participants:

1. Order book liquidation
2. Liquidation queue with vault participation
3. Insurance fund
4. Auto-deleveraging (ADL) as a final backstop

# LIT Utility

Lighter Infrastructure Token (LIT) is the native infrastructure token supporting access, incentives, and alignment across the Lighter ecosystem.

### Staking

The **LIT Staking Pool** (<https://app.lighter.xyz/staking>) is designed to align long-term participants with the core economics of the protocol. By staking LIT, participants gain access to platform benefits aligned with how they interact with the exchange. Unstaking is subject to a 3-day lockup period.

Active Staking Programs:

* LLP Access
* Staking APR

#### LLP Access

As part of our approach to offering access to niche financial products, the Lighter Liquidity Pool (LLP) is now exclusively accessible to LIT stakers. For every 1 LIT staked, participants may deposit up to 10 USDC into the LLP.

#### Staking APR

Staking participants currently earn a fixed 6% APR through staking rewards. LIT is bought from `0xADbE1265C0df1B623A56d324De494Bcb8e8914Ff` for these rewards.

### Buybacks

LIT is bought back by the protocol using trading fee revenue. Buybacks are executed via daily 24-hour TWAPs, with the flexibility to use shorter timeframes depending on market conditions.

The treasury account that conducts these is `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`

# Lighter on Robinhood Chain Points

The Lighter Points Program on the Robinhood Chain is a way to recognize eligible users for participating in the trading platform and reward them for the value they bring.

Points are calculated and awarded in real time based on eligible activity, with an additional weekly points drop every Friday (first weekly drop on Fri Aug 21). The way points are calculated may change over time as we continue improving the program and rewarding meaningful participation while keeping things fair for everyone.

### Live & Weekly Points

The live points are distributed in real time based on factors like volume, positions held, fees paid, using assets other than USDG as collateral, and others. Most markets have the same weight.

Weekly points are based on the activity from the previous Friday (incl.) to Thursday (incl.), are distributed every Friday, and are fine-tuned depending on the week’s activity.

For both point types, standard-to-standard activity is not rewarded.

### Boosts

There are several ways for a user to boost their points. Some apply to both live and weekly points; others apply only to weekly points.

#### Robinhood Wallet Mobile boost

The mobile boost is linear and ranges from 1x for a user with only non-RH wallet mobile app volume to 2x for a user with only RH wallet volume. The volume is considered coming from the plaftorm that the order was placed from.

The boost influences both live and weekly points.

#### Referral boost

If you refer a trader, you get 10% of their points (live + weekly).

Referred traders get a 10% boost for their weekly points.

#### Market boosts

Some markets generate more points than others. Some do so for live points, some for the weekly, some for both.

A notable current boost is the earnings boost for weekly points: if an RWA market is tied to a company that does its earnings call in the interval the weekly points are calculated for, that market is boosted.

Pre IPO markets and new listings may also get boosts.

#### Hedge boost

The hedge boost allows traders to hedge (some of) their Lighter RH positions on Lighter Core and get more points for it.

For each market present on both venues, the 2.5x boost only applies to one pair of directions (e.g. long Core, short RH) out of the two.

A partial hedge also counts: if your position on Lighter RH is $100, but you're only hedged for $50 on Lighter Core, you will get a 1.75x boost. Otherwise, if the (opposing) position on Core is the same or larger, you get the complete boost.

The hedge boost only applies to weekly points and can be updated weekly. We consider the following categories for the boost, with directions specified below.

**W12 (Oct 30 - Nov 5)**

| Category                     | (Lighter) Core | (Lighter) RH | Boost |
| ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------ | ----- |
| **Crypto**                   | Short          | Long         | 2.5x  |
| **RWA (Commodities, ETFs)**  | Short          | Long         | 2.5x  |
| **RWA (Pre IPOs, Equities)** | Long           | Short        | 2.5x  |

**W13 (Nov 6 - Nov 12)**

| Category                     | (Lighter) Core | (Lighter) RH | Boost |
| ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------ | ----- |
| **Crypto**                   | Short          | Long         | 2.5x  |
| **RWA (Commodities, ETFs)**  | Short          | Long         | 2.5x  |
| **RWA (Pre IPOs, Equities)** | Short          | Long         | 2.5x  |

### Support

If you have any questions about this program, please open a ticket in the Lighter Discord server.

Lighter Discord server: <https://discord.gg/lighterxyz>

These Terms govern eligibility for the Lighter on the Robinhood Chain Points Program (the "Program"). By participating in the Program, you agree to these Terms.

The purpose of the Program is to reward genuine participation on Lighter on the Robinhood Chain. Points are intended to recognize authentic trading activity and meaningful participation in the ecosystem—not activity designed to manipulate or exploit the Program.

### 1. General Eligibility

Lighter on the Robinhood Chain determines, in its sole discretion, whether activity is eligible to earn points.

### 2. Ineligible Activity

The following activities are not eligible to receive points and may result in point adjustments, disqualification, or removal from the Program.

#### A. Market Manipulation

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Wash trading.
* Self-trading or trading between commonly controlled accounts.
* Artificially inflating trading volume or liquidity.
* Coordinated trading intended to manipulate markets or Program metrics.
* Spoofing, layering, quote stuffing, or other deceptive trading practices.
* Any activity intended to create artificial or misleading market activity.

#### B. Sybil Activity

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Operating or controlling multiple accounts to earn additional points.
* Splitting activity across multiple accounts to increase rewards.
* Creating, purchasing, renting, borrowing, or otherwise controlling accounts for the purpose of farming points.
* Any attempt to disguise common ownership or coordinated control of accounts.

#### C. Referral Abuse

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Self-referrals.
* Circular or reciprocal referral schemes.
* Creating accounts solely to generate referral rewards.
* Artificially inflating referral activity or referral-based rewards.

#### D. Automated or Artificial Participation

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Activity primarily intended to farm points rather than participate in markets.
* Using bots, scripts, or automated systems to manipulate Program metrics.
* Coordinated behavior designed to exploit the Program or its scoring methodology.

#### E. Abuse of Program Mechanics

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Exploiting bugs, vulnerabilities, or unintended behavior.
* Circumventing Program rules or safeguards.
* Manipulating snapshots, scoring methodologies, or eligibility calculations.
* Any activity intended to obtain points in a manner inconsistent with the purpose of the Program.

#### F. Fraudulent or Unlawful Conduct

This includes, but is not limited to:

* Fraud, deception, impersonation, or identity abuse.
* Providing false, misleading, or inaccurate information.
* Using stolen, compromised, or unauthorized accounts.
* Activity that violates applicable law or the Terms of Service of Lighter on the Robinhood Chain.

### 3. Ongoing Integrity Reviews

To protect the integrity of the Program, \*\*Lighter \*\* continuously performs automated and manual reviews, including Sybil detection, fraud detection, behavioral analysis, and other integrity checks.

These reviews may occur at any time during the Program or after it has concluded.

The fact that points have been awarded or remain visible in an account does not mean they have been permanently approved or are no longer subject to review.

### 4. Point Adjustments and Enforcement

If Lighter determines that an account has engaged in fraudulent, abusive, manipulative, or otherwise ineligible activity, Lighter may, at any time and in its sole discretion:

* Remove or reduce points.
* Reverse previously awarded points.
* Disqualify specific transactions or activity from earning points.
* Suspend or permanently remove an account from the Program.
* Exclude an account from future rewards, distributions, or Program benefits.

These actions may be taken before, during, or after points have been awarded, including after the conclusion of the Program if subsequent reviews identify activity that is determined to be fraudulent, abusive, manipulative, or otherwise ineligible.

### 5. Final Determination

Lighter on the Robinhood Chain reserves the right to interpret these Terms and determine Program eligibility in its sole discretion.

The examples listed in these Terms are illustrative and not exhaustive. Any activity that Lighter on the Robinhood Chain reasonably believes undermines the fairness, integrity, or intended purpose of the Program may be deemed ineligible, even if not specifically described above.

Participation in the Program constitutes acceptance of these Terms and any updates or modifications published by Lighter on the Robinhood Chain.

- [Order Types](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types.md): Choose from classic order types and strategies based on how you want to trade.
- [Classic](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic.md): Choose a market, limit, stop, RFQ, TWAP or Scale order to control price and timing.
- [Market](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/market.md): Execute at available market prices when you want to enter or exit promptly.
- [Limit](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/limit.md): Set the price you are willing to trade at and choose how unfilled orders are handled.
- [Stop Market](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/stop-market.md): Place a market order when a trigger price is reached, for a stop loss, take profit or entry.
- [Stop Limit](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/stop-limit.md): Combine a price trigger with a limit price for the order placed when it triggers.
- [RFQ](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/rfq.md): Request liquidity and review an estimate before submitting a market order.
- [TWAP](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/twap.md): Spread an order over 1 minute to 24 hours using smaller market orders placed over time.
- [Scale](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/classic/scale.md): Place up to 100 limit orders across a price range from one form, with control over how prices and sizes are distributed.
- [Strategies](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies.md): Use price tracking, conditional triggers, sequential execution or baskets to manage more complex orders.
- [Chase](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/chase.md): Automatically reprice a post-only limit order to follow the best bid or ask while seeking a maker fill.
- [Conditional Market](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/conditional-market.md): Place a market order when a chosen market meets a price condition, including a trigger on a different market.
- [Conditional Limit](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/conditional-limit.md): Place a limit order when a chosen market meets a price condition, with control over the limit price and time-in-force.
- [OCO (One-Cancels-the-Other)](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/oco.md): Set two alternative stop orders so that the first to trigger cancels the other.
- [Trailing Stop](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/trailing-stop.md): Track a market with a stop at a fixed percentage or dollar distance, then place a market order when the price reverses.
- [Swarm](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/swarm.md): Split an order into small market orders placed in quick succession, with optional randomization and a price boundary.
- [Trigger Swarm](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/trigger-swarm.md): Wait for a price condition, then place an amount as a sequence of small market orders, one at a time.
- [Atomic](https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/order-types/strategies/atomic.md): Submit a weighted basket of market orders together for a pair trade or a position across several markets.

- [REST API](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api.md)
- [Markets](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets.md): This section covers details for interacting with all perpetual futures markets listed on Pacifica.
- [Get Market Info](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-market-info.md): This endpoint allows users to get exchange information, including market specifications for all available trading pairs.
- [Get Prices](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-prices.md): This endpoint allows users to get price information for all symbols, including mark prices, funding rates, and market statistics.
- [Get Candle Data](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-candle-data.md): This endpoint allows users to get historical price candles for a specific market and time interval.
- [Get Mark Price Candle Data](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-mark-price-candle-data.md): This endpoint allows users to get historical mark price candles for a specific market and time interval.
- [Get Orderbook](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-orderbook.md): This endpoint allows users to retrieve the current orderbook (bid/ask levels) for a specified trading symbol.
- [Get Recent Trades](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-recent-trades.md): This endpoint allows users to get recent trades for a specific market.
- [Get Historical Funding](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-historical-funding.md): This endpoint retrieves the historical funding for a particular symbol
- [Get Fee Levels](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-fee-levels.md): This endpoint returns all fee level tiers and their corresponding maker and taker fee rates.
- [Get Loan Pool](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/markets/get-loan-pool.md): This endpoint returns the current state of the loan pool including utilization, borrow and lend rates.
- [Account](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account.md): This section covers details for interacting with user accounts on Pacifica.
- [Get Account Info](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-account-info.md): This endpoint allows users to get all high-level account info such as balance, fee level, equity, etc.
- [Get Account Settings](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-account-settings.md): This endpoint allows users to get account margin and leverage settings (if they are not at default values)
- [Update Account Settings](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/update-account-settings.md): This endpoint allows users to update account settings, such as their leaderboard privacy mode.
- [Update Leverage](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/update-leverage.md): This endpoint allows users to change their account leverage for a specific trading pair. For open positions, users can only increase the leverage setting.
- [Update Margin Mode](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/update-margin-mode.md): This endpoint allows users to switch between isolated and cross margin modes for a specific trading pair. For open positions, users cannot change the margin mode.
- [Get Positions](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-positions.md): This endpoint allows users to get current positions.
- [Get Trade History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-trade-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get trade history
- [Get Funding History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-funding-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get funding history.
- [Get Account Equity History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-account-equity-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get account equity and PnL history (over time).
- [Get Account Balance History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-account-balance-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get account balance history. Returns all balance effects that affect the queried account.
- [Request Withdrawal](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/request-withdrawal.md): This endpoint allows users to request withdrawal.
- [Get Account Loan Info](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-account-loan-info.md): This endpoint returns loan and collateral information for a given account under unified margin.
- [Add Isolated Margin](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/add-isolated-margin.md): This endpoint allows users to add margin to an isolated position.
- [Update Spot Settings](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/update-spot-settings.md): This endpoint allows users to update spot asset settings for unified margin.
- [Toggle Auto-Lending](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/toggle-auto-lending.md): This endpoint allows users to enable or disable automatic lending.
- [Get Spot Balance History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-spot-balance-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get spot asset balance history.
- [Withdraw Spot Asset](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/withdraw-spot-asset.md): This endpoint allows users to withdraw a spot asset.
- [Get Pending Spot Withdrawals](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-pending-spot-withdrawals.md): This endpoint returns pending spot asset withdrawals.
- [Get Spot Deposit History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-spot-deposit-history.md): This endpoint returns spot asset deposit history.
- [Get Spot Withdrawal History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/account/get-spot-withdrawal-history.md): This endpoint returns spot asset withdrawal history.
- [Two-Factor Authentication](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor.md): This section covers two-factor authentication (2FA) for withdrawals and factor changes.
- [Get Two-Factor Status](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/get-two-factor-status.md): This endpoint allows users to get an account's two-factor status, factors, and remaining recovery keys.
- [Begin TOTP Enrollment](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/begin-totp-enrollment.md): This endpoint allows users to start adding an authenticator app (TOTP) factor.
- [Finish TOTP Enrollment](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/finish-totp-enrollment.md): This endpoint allows users to confirm an authenticator app (TOTP) factor with a code.
- [Begin WebAuthn Registration](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/begin-webauthn-registration.md): This endpoint allows users to start registering a passkey or security key.
- [Finish WebAuthn Registration](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/finish-webauthn-registration.md): This endpoint allows users to finish registering a passkey or security key.
- [Begin WebAuthn Authentication](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/begin-webauthn-authentication.md): This endpoint allows users to get a challenge for a passkey or security key proof.
- [Disable Two-Factor Authentication](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/disable-two-factor.md): This endpoint allows users to turn off two-factor authentication and delete every factor and recovery key.
- [Remove Factor](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/remove-factor.md): This endpoint allows users to remove one factor.
- [Rename Factor](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/rename-factor.md): This endpoint allows users to change a factor's label.
- [Regenerate Recovery Keys](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/two-factor/regenerate-recovery-keys.md): This endpoint allows users to replace their recovery keys with a new set.
- [Notifications](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications.md): This section covers push notifications to the mobile app and to browsers, notification preferences, and the in-app notification history.
- [Register Expo Device](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/register-expo-device.md): This endpoint allows users to register an Expo push token so that the mobile app receives push notifications.
- [Unregister Expo Device](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/unregister-expo-device.md): This endpoint allows users to stop push notifications to an Expo push token or app installation.
- [Get Web Push Config](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/get-web-push-config.md): This endpoint allows users to check if Web Push is available and to get the VAPID public key.
- [Register Web Push Subscription](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/register-web-push-subscription.md): This endpoint allows users to register a browser's Web Push subscription.
- [Get Web Push Subscription Status](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/get-web-push-subscription-status.md): This endpoint allows users to check if a browser installation gets Web Push notifications.
- [Unregister Web Push Subscription](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/unregister-web-push-subscription.md): This endpoint allows users to stop Web Push notifications to a browser installation.
- [List Notification Preferences](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/list-notification-preferences.md): This endpoint allows users to get the notification channels that are on for an account.
- [Set Notification Preference](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/set-notification-preference.md): This endpoint allows users to turn a channel on or off for one or more notification types.
- [Set Notification Master Preference](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/set-notification-master-preference.md): This endpoint allows users to turn a channel on or off with the account's master switch.
- [Send Test Notification](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/send-test-notification.md): This endpoint allows users to send a test notification on the account's enabled channels.
- [Get Notification History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/get-notification-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get an account's recent in-app notifications and unread count.
- [Mark Notifications Seen](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/notifications/mark-notifications-seen.md): This endpoint allows users to mark notifications as seen.
- [Vaults](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults.md): REST API endpoints for creating, funding, configuring, and listing vaults.
- [Create Vault](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/create-vault.md): Create a new vault (lake) and optionally set its initial configuration and seed deposit.
- [Claim Vault Referral Code](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/claim-vault-referral-code.md): Claim a referral code for an existing vault.
- [Deposit to Vault](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/deposit-to-vault.md): Deposit funds into a vault and receive vault shares.
- [Claim Vault Manager](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/claim-vault-manager.md): Claim the manager role on a fresh vault.
- [Withdraw From Vault](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/withdraw-from-vault.md): Redeem vault shares and withdraw funds from a vault.
- [Update Vault Deposit Cap](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/update-vault-deposit-cap.md): Update or clear the deposit cap for a vault.
- [Add Vault Whitelist](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/add-vault-whitelist.md): Add tradable symbols to a vault whitelist.
- [Remove Vault Whitelist](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/remove-vault-whitelist.md): Remove tradable symbols from a vault whitelist.
- [Add Vault Blacklist](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/add-vault-blacklist.md): Add blocked symbols to a vault blacklist.
- [Remove Vault Blacklist](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/remove-vault-blacklist.md): Remove blocked symbols from a vault blacklist.
- [Add Vault Max Leverage](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/add-vault-max-leverage.md): Add per-symbol max leverage limits for a vault.
- [Remove Vault Max Leverage](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/remove-vault-max-leverage.md): Remove per-symbol max leverage limits from a vault.
- [List Vaults](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/vaults/list-vaults.md): List all vaults and optionally include the querying account's share balance.
- [Subaccounts](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/subaccounts.md)
- [Create Subaccount](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/subaccounts/create-subaccount.md): This endpoint allows regular accounts to create subaccounts with a secure authentication scheme. Both the main account and subaccount must sign to establish the relationship.
- [List Subaccounts](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/subaccounts/list-subaccounts.md): Lists all subaccounts associated with a main (parent) account. Returns address, balance, and other account details for each subaccount.
- [Subaccount Fund Transfer](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/subaccounts/subaccount-fund-transfer.md): This endpoint allows transfer of funds between main and subaccounts
- [Subaccount Spot Transfer](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/subaccounts/subaccount-spot-transfer.md): This endpoint allows users to transfer spot assets between a main account and its subaccounts
- [Spot](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/spot.md)
- [Get Spot Assets](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/spot/get-spot-assets.md): This endpoint returns a list of all spot assets available on the exchange, including their trading parameters and collateral eligibility.
- [Get Bridge Info](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/spot/get-bridge-info.md): This endpoint returns bridge parameters for all spot assets, including deposit minimums, withdrawal fees, and on-chain program addresses.
- [Get Bridge Parameters](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/spot/get-bridge-parameters.md): This endpoint returns bridge parameters for a single spot asset by symbol, including deposit minimums, withdrawal fees, and on-chain program addresses.
- [Orders](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders.md): This section covers details for interacting with current and historical orders on Pacifica.
- [Create Market Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/create-market-order.md): This endpoint allows users to create a new market order with optional take profit and stop loss levels.
- [Create Limit Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/create-limit-order.md): This endpoint allows users to create a new limit order with optional take profit and stop loss levels.
- [Create Stop Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/create-stop-order.md): This endpoint allows users to create stop order.
- [Create Position TP/SL](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/create-position-tp-sl.md): This endpoint allows users to set take profit and stop loss levels for an existing position.
- [Cancel Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/cancel-order.md): This endpoint allows users to cancel an existing order.
- [Cancel All Orders](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/cancel-all-orders.md): This endpoint allows users to cancel all orders for all/given symbol(s).
- [Cancel Stop Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/cancel-stop-order.md): This endpoint allows users to cancel a stop order by its (CL)OID.
- [Edit Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/edit-order.md): This endpoint allows users to edit an existing limit order by modifying its size and/or price.
- [Batch Order](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/batch-order.md): This endpoint allows users to submit multiple order operations in a single request. Batched orders are executed in the order they are batched in, and will not be split up by other users' orders.
- [Get Open Orders](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/get-open-orders.md): This endpoint allows users to get open orders on their account.
- [Get Order History](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/get-order-history.md): This endpoint allows users to get a summarized order history.
- [Get Order History by ID](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/get-order-history-by-id.md): This endpoint allows users to get order history by id.
- [Get Order History Records](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/orders/get-order-history-records.md): This endpoint allows users to get order history and finished order strategies in one list.
- [Order Strategies](https://docs.pacifica.fi/api-documentation/api/rest-api/order-strategies.md): This section covers server-side order strategies such as OCO, conditional, trailing stop, chase, swarm, and TWAP orders.

# Print

Print lets you earn yield while your orders wait to be filled. Instead of a limit order that sits idle until the market reaches it, a Print order pays you for every cycle it waits — and still opens your position at the exact price you chose.

### How Print Works

You set a **target price** and a **direction**:

* **Print Long** — target price *below* the current market ("if BTC drops to X, I'll buy").
* **Print Short** — target price *above* the current market ("if BTC rises to X, I'll sell").

You lock a deposit, pick your leverage, and choose how long each cycle runs — **24 hours** on any market, or **7 days** or **30 days** on BTC. From there you earn a payout every cycle while you wait. Your order isn't filled the moment the market touches your target — it's checked once at the end of each cycle: if the market has reached your target by then, it fills at your target price; if not, it rolls into the next cycle and keeps earning.

![A 24-hour Print order earns yield at every checkpoint while it waits, then fills at your target price](https://mintcdn.com/pacifica-fi-docs-migrate-92/kheiedfGyimX38EQ/images/print-how-it-works.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=kheiedfGyimX38EQ\&q=85\&s=3c54797b43349ebb02544925305d553d)

Print is available on **BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, ZEC, XRP, LIT, NEAR, ENA, and SKHYNIX**. Every listed Print market offers a 24-hour cycle; BTC also offers 7-day and 30-day cycles. See [Specifications](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/specifications.md) for current leverage and deposit limits.

### Print vs. Limit Orders

Like a limit order, you pick a side, a target price, and a leverage. What's different is everything about *waiting* and *filling*:

| | Limit order | Print order |
| - | - | - |
| Earn while waiting | No | Yes — a payout every cycle |
| When it can fill | The instant the market touches your price, any time | Only at the **end of each cycle** |
| Fill price | Your limit price | Your target price |
| If the price never reaches it | Rests unchanged until you cancel | Auto-rolls to a new target at the same % distance, and keeps earning |
| Capital while waiting | Reserved, earns nothing | Locked as margin, and earns yield every cycle |
| Cancelling | Removed immediately | Resolves at the end of the current cycle |

The most important difference: a limit order fills the moment price touches it. **A Print order only checks at the end of each cycle.** If the market dips to your target intraday and bounces back, a limit order would have filled — a Print order does not. It only fills if the market has reached or passed your target *at the checkpoint*.

### In This Section

* [Placing & Managing Orders](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/placing-and-managing-orders.md) — the inputs you set, and how to cancel or withdraw.
* [The Print Cycle](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/the-print-cycle.md) — how fills and roll-overs work, and what cycle length changes.
* [Yield](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/yield.md) — how your payout is calculated and what drives it.
* [Margin & Liquidation](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/margin-and-liquidation.md) — leverage, liquidation price, and your maximum loss.
* [Examples](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/examples.md) — worked scenarios with real numbers.
* [Specifications](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/specifications.md) — markets, limits, and parameters at a glance.
* [FAQ](https://docs.pacifica.fi/print/faq.md) — common questions.

# Points Program

The Pacifica Points program launched on Thursday, September 4th at 00:00 UTC. Each week:

* Snapshots are taken every Thursday at 00:00 UTC
* Distributions occur within 24 hours of each snapshot
* Weekly allocation: 10,000,000 points distributed weekly among eligible Pacifica users

Earn points by engaging in organic trading activities on Pacifica via GUI or API. Self-trading, sybil or any other manipulative activities will not earn points.\

![](https://mintcdn.com/pacifica-fi-docs-migrate-92/g3zlaiQhnLQgGHk6/images/nxYqgMZnitxZPYZy5gnQ.jpg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=g3zlaiQhnLQgGHk6\&q=85\&s=dcda13705e4afc6aad7d0fb8b582398c)

### FAQ

#### What Is the Pacifica Points Formula?

The formula is dynamic and opaque by design, updated weekly as usage evolves.

#### What Activities Earn Points?

Many activities are tracked by our points program, and attribution for different activities may happen immediately or be applied over-time over several distributions.

#### Who Knows the Details of the Points Program?

Very few Pacifica team members. Only Pacifica's community members are eligible to earn points in order to ensure fairness and prevent abuse.

#### Do People With Multiple Accounts Have an Advantage Over Me?

No. Discrete or costless actions do not yield rewards in isolation. Having 100 accounts provides no advantage over one.

#### Do Early Users Have an Advantage?

Pacifica's points program is structured to balance both early supporters and long-term contributors fairly.

#### Can I Buy Points?

No. There was no prior allocation and there is no way to purchase points. They can only be earned by trading, providing feedback, and spreading the word.

#### Can I Trade Points on Secondary Markets?

While Pacifica cannot/will not actively police this, we do not condone any such activity and strongly discourage this for security reasons.

# Fees

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Lifetime lowest fee tier for existing depositors**
>
> Starting at **00:01 UTC on Monday, 24 August 2026**, all users who have
> already deposited will receive our lowest fee tier for life on the following
> products:
>
> `USA500`, `SKHYNIX`, `US100`, `SPCX`, `SNDK`, `GOOGL`, `NVDA`, `MU`, `SKHY`,
> `INTC`, `SAMSUNG`, `NBIS`, `CRCL`, `CBRS`, `META`, `TSLA`, `MRVL`, `AAPL`,
> `AMZN`, `MSFT`, and `MSTR`.
>
> This means **0 bps maker fees** on all listed products, with taker fees of
> **1.5 bps for equities** and **0.6 bps for indices**.

QFEX uses a maker-taker fee model for determining its trading fees. Orders that provide liquidity (maker orders) are charged different fees than orders that take liquidity (taker orders). Fees are calculated based on the current pricing tier you are in when the order is placed, and not on the tier you would be in after a trade is completed. Your fee tier is based upon total USD trading volume over the trailing 30 day period.

Transactions made on books quoted in USD, e.g. EUR-USD, are counted as the total USD amount of each filled order.

When you place an order at the market price that gets filled immediately, you are considered a taker and will pay a fee between 0.006% and 0.10%. When you place an order which is not immediately matched by an existing order, that order is placed on the order book. If another customer places an order that matches yours, you are considered the maker and will pay a fee between 0.00% and 0.10%.

When you place an order that gets partially matched immediately, you pay a taker fee for that portion. The remainder of the order is placed on the order book and, when matched, is considered a maker order. You pay a maker fee for this remaining portion of the total order.

Please note that the pricing tiers can take some time to update. For future orders, we recommend checking your fee tier before you trade to ensure you are in the updated pricing tier.

Integrators can earn a share of trading fees with a [builder code](https://docs.qfex.com/qfex/builder-code.md). Traders attach the code on the Trade WebSocket [auth message](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/authenticate.md); the trader still pays the full fee, and the builder's configured share is credited as builder rewards.

There are five tiers of fees, based on your Effective Volume for a trailing 30-day period traded on the platform. Effective Volume is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{Effective Volume} = 2 \times \text{Commodities} + 2 \times \text{Indices} + 5 \times \text{Single stocks}
$$

Where:

* Commodities = volume traded against commodities futures (eg Gold)

# Changelog

> Product updates and announcements

**29th October 2026**

Trade WebSocket documentation correction

Corrected the [Balances](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/balance.md) and [Positions](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/positions.md) references and Trade Playground schema: both channels have a 60-second periodic refresh plus event-driven updates.

Documented immediate cached snapshots on subscription and coalesced updates when placing or cancelling orders changes reserved margin. Clarified that subscribers receive `balance_response` and per-symbol `position_response` snapshots, and removed the obsolete v4 envelopes from the Trade schema. This corrects the documentation; it does not announce a protocol change.

**1st November 2026**

Fix

**Reference data now populates underlier\_price and price\_change\_24h.**

Endpoints: `GET /refdata`.

underlier\_price returns the latest available underlier price. price\_change\_24h returns the rolling 24-hour percentage change in mark price using minute-resolution history, rounded to eight decimal places. Mark prices are refreshed at most once every 30 seconds. Missing or invalid prices and unavailable history remain empty strings, and reference metadata remains available if the price lookup fails.

**1st November 2026**

New Endpoint

**Public reference-market holiday calendar.**

Endpoints: `GET /market-holidays`.

Returns holidays from a generated snapshot of the Entimos Slack calendar for inclusive date ranges up to 366 days, with an optional market filter. Includes coverage windows and incomplete markets so missing schedules are explicit. These dates are not QFEX trading halts or instrument-specific session times.

**1st November 2026**

Docs Update

**Link public market hours, holidays, and earnings and economic calendars.**

Endpoints: `GET /refdata`, `GET /calendar`.

Clarify that symbol market hours are available in refdata without authentication and cross-link the public calendar endpoints in their operation descriptions.

**30th October 2026**

Breaking Change

**Publish API version 2026-10-30 with source-free earnings metadata.**

Endpoints: `GET /calendar`.

The latest API contract is now 2026-10-30. Calendar earnings metadata omits source, sources, source\_name and source\_url keys, including nested release-time attribution. Financial results, release timing and economic events are unchanged. The 2026-10-29 contract preserves its original response.

**Migration:** Pin api\_version=2026-10-29 to keep earnings attribution. Omitted api\_version, latest and 2026-10-30 select the new response. Clients using earnings sources must pin the previous version or stop relying on those fields.

**30th October 2026**

New Endpoint

**Public earnings and economic calendar endpoint.**

Endpoints: `GET /calendar`.

Returns earnings and economic events for an inclusive from/to date range of up to 93 days without authentication. Economic events include the last successful sync timestamp and stale status. Missing financial results and release times remain null. Invalid ranges are rejected and upstream failures return 503. CloudFront caching is capped at five minutes and varies only by api\_version, from and to query parameters, with hostname and CORS-origin separation.

**29th October 2026**

New Endpoint

**Select a dated REST API contract with the api\_version query parameter.**

Omitting api\_version or using latest selects the latest contract. The first published contract is 2026-10-29. Unsupported, empty, or repeated versions return HTTP 400. Qfex-Api-Version reports the selected contract. OpenAPI exports accept the same selector, and documentation and schema links have stable dated metadata URLs.

**27th October 2026**

Breaking Change

**Builder wallet messages accept a website domain and default to qfex.com.**

Endpoints: `GET /builder/web3/message`.

The optional domain query parameter accepts non-QFEX hostnames and sets the message domain and HTTPS URI. If the domain is not provided  the default website uri in the message is [www.qfex.com](http://www.qfex.com). Browser access still requires the website origin in the API CORS configuration. Registration requires the generated URI in the Supabase Auth Redirect URLs allowlist.

**Migration:** Pass domain=[www.qfex.com](http://www.qfex.com) to retain the previous message domain, or supply your website hostname without a scheme, path, port, or credentials.

**23rd October 2026**

New Endpoint

**Isolated positions now expose cash collateral separately from equity.**

Endpoints: `GET /user/positions`.

Isolated positions include isolated\_collateral, which excludes unrealised PnL and includes settled fees, funding and realised PnL. Their existing margin field continues to report equity including unrealised PnL.

**22nd October 2026**

New Endpoint

**Symbol reference data now includes isolated\_only.**

Endpoints: `GET /refdata`.

Each symbol returns an explicit boolean indicating whether it requires isolated margin. Flagged symbols require isolated route registration before trading. Existing cross exposure can still be cancelled or closed with reduce-only orders.

**14th October 2026**

API Update

**Initial invitation qualification now uses lifetime personal trading volume.**

Endpoints: `POST /user/invitation-codes/job`, `GET /user/referrals/notional-volume`.

Creators receive their initial five invitations after reaching \$100,000 of all-time personal trading volume, including subaccounts, rather than volume in the last 14 days. The qualification responses add self\_lifetime\_notional\_volume; existing self\_notional\_volume remains the 14-day value. Referred volume does not count toward initial qualification. Existing grants and recurring invitation rules are unchanged.

**13th October 2026**

Docs Update

**REST API release notes now follow production deployments.**

Public REST API changes now appear in the REST API changelog after the corresponding API revision is available in production. The reference is rebuilt from the production OpenAPI document with each tracked release.

**13th October 2026**

Breaking Change

**Builder Web3 signed messages now link to the QFEX Client Agreement.**

Endpoints: `GET /builder/web3/message`, `POST /builder/web3/api-key`.

The legal consent statement includes [https://docs.qfex.com/legal/client-agreement](https://docs.qfex.com/legal/client-agreement.md) beside the Client Agreement. Key issuance requires the updated statement, including this link.

**Migration:** Request and sign a fresh message from GET /builder/web3/message. Submit that string unchanged to POST /builder/web3/api-key; messages without the agreement link are rejected.

**13th October 2026**

Breaking Change

**Builder Web3 registration now includes legal consent and an Arbitrum withdrawal address.**

Endpoints: `GET /builder/web3/message`, `POST /builder/web3/api-key`.

The signed message now authorizes a trading API key and includes acceptance of the QFEX Client Agreement, Privacy Policy, and Cookie Policy. Messages without this consent are rejected. Successful key issuance records the acceptance date and registers the verified wallet address on ARBITRUM\_ONE without duplicating an existing address.

**Migration:** Request a fresh message from GET /builder/web3/message and sign the returned string unchanged before submitting it to POST /builder/web3/api-key. Clients that construct messages themselves must include the updated consent statement.

**14th October 2026**

Market Data Update

`market_stats` wildcard subscriptions (`symbols: ["*"]`) now receive all-symbol snapshots every 10 seconds. Named-symbol subscriptions continue to update once per second. An initial snapshot is sent on subscription when data is available.

The [Market Stats reference](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/mds/market_stats.md) and MDS Playground schema now document funding rates, rolling 24-hour traded quantity, and rolling 24-hour USD notional volume.

**9th September 2026**

Breaking Change

`modify_order` now requires the `reduce_only` field. It must match the order being modified, as a modify cannot change reduce-only.

Requests that omit it are rejected with `InvalidJSONFormat`, and a value that does not match the resting order is rejected with `CANNOT_MODIFY_NO_SUCH_ORDER`.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/modify_order.md) for further details

**7th September 2026**

Docs Update

Added builder codes: create and view a code over REST, then attach it on the Trade WebSocket auth message as `params.builder_code`. Public balances expose credited share as `builder_rewards`.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/qfex/builder-code.md) and [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/authenticate.md) for further details

**17th February 2026**

Docs Update

Added default\_max\_leverage field to refdata response.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/mds/refdata.md) for further details

**9th February 2026**

Docs Update

Added funding scaling documentation. The final funding rate is now documented as scaled by `1/100`, and the funding stream reflects the post-scaling value.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/mds/funding_rate.md), [here](https://docs.qfex.com/qfex/contract-specifications.md), and [here](https://docs.qfex.com/qfex/faq.md) for further details

**26th January 2026**

Docs Update

Added the `fills` channel and fill response payload documentation.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/fills.md) for further details

**12th November 2025**

Docs Update

Updated trades response to include `execution_type`.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/mds/trades.md) for further details

**12th November 2025**

Docs Update

Updated order response to include trade\_id. This is used for order responses with a status of FILLED, it provides the unique trade id of that fill.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/order.md) for further details

Updated get\_user\_trades endpoint to support more filtering.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/get_user_trades.md) for further details

**30th October 2025**

Docs Update

Updated stop order response type. Type is now `STOP_LOSS` and `TAKE_PROFIT`. Stop orders are shown in the `orders` key in `get_orders_response`

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/get_user_orders.md) and [here](https://docs.qfex.com/api-reference/enums.md) for further details

Docs Update

Added documentation for stop orders.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/stop_add_order.md), [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/stop_modify_order.md) and [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/stop_cancel_order.md) for further details

Docs Update

Added Close Position request.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/close_position.md) for further details

This is only intended for use in the frontend as a quick way to close a position.

Docs Update

Added HMAC-SHA256 authentication requirements for the trade WebSocket, including refreshed client samples.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/authenticate.md) for further details

Documented the new cancel-on-disconnect channel with end-to-end examples for Python, Node.js, Go, and Java.

See [here](https://docs.qfex.com/websocket/channels/trade/cancel_on_disconnect.md) for further details

You must now include order type in a modify order

# FAQ
Frequently asked questions about RISEx
Copy Page Open
## General
### What is RISEx?
RISEx is a fully onchain orderbook DEX built on RISE Chain, supporting perpetual futures (spot markets coming soon). Unlike hybrid exchanges with off-chain matching engines, RISEx executes all orders, matching, and settlement within the EVM.
### What's the relationship between RISEx and RISE?
RISE and RISEx are one team, one vision, one token. RISE is the infrastructure layer that finally supports onchain orderbooks, and RISEx the flagship exchange built on that infrastructure. RISEx will bootstrap activity on RISE and fuel a thriving DeFi ecosystem on RISE.
### When will RISEx be live?
RISEx is live now on gated mainnet.
### How do I get access to the private mainnet?
Get access through:
- Direct invite from the team
- Via our waitlist referral leaderboard
X DMs are open if you want to connect with the team @risextrade
### How is RISEx different from Hyperliquid?
Hyperliquid showed the world what's possible with onchain orderbooks, but it's missing one key structural feature - synchronous composability. Hyperliquid runs on a custom L1 with a separate execution environment. RISEx runs on RISE, an EVM-compatible chain, which means it's synchronously composable with all other DeFi protocols. Your positions can be used as collateral in lending protocols, yield strategies can manage your margin, and builders can integrate permissionlessly. Read more .
### How is RISEx decentralized?
RISEx is powered by RISE, an Ethereum Optimistic L2 which has been fine-tuned to support realtime orderbooks onchain. L2s inherit Ethereum's security for settlement and data availability. Execution is managed by centralised sequencers, however, we are building toward progressive decentralization.
### Is RISEx matching onchain?
All trading logic executes onchain and is verifiable, accessible with a familiar EVM block explorer. There are no off-chain components for matching or settlement.
### Does RISEx support spot trading?
RISEx currently supports perps, spot will come soon. See our roadmap for details.
## Trading
### What leverage is available?
Leverage varies by market. See market configuration for current limits per asset.
### What are the fees?
See the full fee schedule details.
### How fast is execution?
RISE Chain has sub-3ms execution. Cancel orders, for example, are sub-1ms. Orders and trades execute in realtime.
## Technical
### What collateral is accepted?
USDC is the base collateral asset. Portfolio Margin will unlock any ERC20 as collateral once available.
### Is there an API?
Yes! See the API documentation .
### Where are the smart contracts?
See the Contracts page for architecture and addresses.
## Safety
### Is RISEx audited?
Yes. The RISEx exchange contracts were reviewed by Cantina, and the XLP Vault was audited by yAudit. See Audits for the full reports.
### What happens if I get liquidated?
RISEx uses partial liquidations first, giving you the best chance to stay in the market. Liquidation triggers when your health factor falls to 1 or below. See liquidations for details.
### What is health factor?
Health factor = cross_margin_balance / total_maintenance_margin. Above 1 is safe, at or below 1 triggers liquidation.

# Points
The RISE points program and Season 1 Ignite.
Copy Page Open
The RISE points program exists to attract and retain real traders, and to distribute points to the users helping pave the way for RISEx to become a leading exchange.
The program launched with Season 1: Ignite on 20 July 2026 at 00:00 UTC .
Each week, a capped pool of points is split across traders based on their activity on the venue: what you trade, how long you hold, what you pay in fees, your slippage, and who you bring to the venue.
## Season 1: Ignite
Ignite is the first full points seasonlaunches.
- Points begin accruing on 20 July 2026 at 00:00 UTC .
- Points are distributed weekly, with the first distribution at 14:00 UTC on Tuesday, 28 July 2026 .
- 200k points are allocated per weekly distribution.
Ignite is expected to end no later than Q2 2027 , our timelines are aligned with projected major product milestones
## Earning points
Each week, points are allocated based on your share of qualifying activity on RISEx. The points model changes each week. Qualifying activity includes:
- Higher order activity : user segmentation
- Total costs : fees paid, slippage, and negative markouts
- Trading volume : both maker and taker
- Open interest and position hold time
- Referrals : earn an additional 10% of your referee's points
The exact methodology and weightings are not published. This protects the program from being gamed.
## Genesis Traders
Prior to Ignite, RISEx ran without a public points program. Users who traded during that period are allocated retroactive points based on their real activity: what they traded and how they contributed to the venue.
Distribution details for Season 0 will be announced separately. Distribution occurs on Thursday, 23 July 2026 at 14:00 UTC .
## RISE airdrop allocation
100% of RISE points are allocated to RISEx users, including traders, LPs, and builder-code integrators.
Why? RISE is an exchange chain and RISEx is the core product. Other apps built on the chain benefit from RISEx activity because they either:
-
- Leverage RISEx liquidity and features through builder codes, or
-
- RISEx is a user of their product, such as lending or AMM backstop liquidity, benefiting from the distribution and activity that trading generates
Early RISE supporters will receive additional benefits within the RISE points program.

# TxFlow Docs

> TxFlow is a layer-1 exchange for perpetuals and prediction (Outcome) markets. These docs cover trading mechanics, the protocol core, and the API: `POST /info` reads, WebSocket streams, and EIP-712–signed `POST /exchange` writes.

Every page below is plain Markdown, with API schemas fully expanded. Links are relative to the host serving this file. [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) has all of them in one file. For an integration, read Builder API Reference → Signing → the reference pages you need, and follow the rules in the appendix.

- [What is TxFlow](/index.md)

## Introduction

- [Key Concepts](/introduction/key-concepts.md): The vocabulary the rest of these docs assume: accounts, instruments, channels, margin, prices, and networks.

## Getting Started

- [Start Trading](/getting-started/start-trading.md): Connect with email, social or your own wallet, deposit USDC, enable trading, and place your first order on TxFlow.
- [Deposits & Withdrawals](/getting-started/deposits-and-withdrawals.md): Move USDC collateral and spot assets in and out of TxFlow, from a wallet, a CEX, or another chain.
- [Export your email wallet](/getting-started/export-email-wallet.md): Export the private key or seed phrase of the wallet TxFlow created for your email login
- [Ecosystem](/getting-started/ecosystem.md): Explorers, tools, and apps built on TxFlow

## Trade

- [Trading on TxFlow](/trade.md): How trading works from a trader's point of view: the mechanics, formulas, and worked examples behind margin, liquidation, funding, and fees.
- [Margin & Leverage](/trade/margin-and-leverage.md): Margin is the collateral that backs your perpetual positions.
- [Entry Price & PnL](/trade/entry-price-and-pnl.md): Your entry price is the reference point for every profit-and-loss number you see.
- [Liquidation](/trade/liquidation.md): Liquidation closes a position that can no longer meet its maintenance margin.
- [Auto-deleveraging (ADL)](/trade/adl.md): When a liquidation can't be cleared on the order book, the protocol falls back to auto-deleveraging (ADL): the position is closed against traders holding the opposite side.
- [Funding](/trade/funding.md): Perpetuals have no expiry, so a periodic funding payment between longs and shorts keeps the contract price anchored to the oracle price.
- [Mark vs. Oracle Price](/trade/mark-and-index-price.md): A perpetual has more than one "price." Knowing which one drives what protects you from surprises around liquidation and funding.
- [Orders & Time-in-Force](/trade/orders.md): The order types and time-in-force options available across spot, perpetual, and outcome markets, from a trader's standpoint.
- [Contract Specifications](/trade/contract-specifications.md): TxFlow perpetuals are linear derivatives with no expiration date.
- [Position & Order Limits](/trade/position-and-order-limits.md): The ceilings an order has to clear before it reaches the book: a per-market position cap, order size bounds, price bands relative to the oracle, and slippage protection on market orders.
- [Fees & Discounts](/trade/fees.md): What you pay to trade, how the maker/taker split works, and how volume lowers your rate.
- [Deposit & Withdrawal Fees](/trade/deposit-and-withdrawal-fees.md): What you pay to move USDC in and out of TxFlow.
- [Fee Credits](/trade/fee-credits.md): Platform-issued vouchers that reimburse your perp trading fees.
- [Referral](/trade/referral.md): How to unlock your referral code, how many people you can invite, and what both sides earn.
- [Affiliate](/trade/affiliate.md): A multi-tier version of the Referral program for KOLs, agencies, and professional marketers.
- [Vaults](/trade/vaults.md): A vault is a pooled `USDC` account that trades a strategy and shares the result with its depositors.

## Prediction Markets

- [Prediction Markets](/prediction/overview.md): How prediction markets price probability, how payouts settle at 1 or 0, and how they differ from perpetuals.
- [Market Types](/prediction/market-types.md): TxFlow lists prediction markets with two outcome structures: binary (two outcomes) and category (several outcomes, one winner).
- [Trading Prediction Markets](/prediction/trading.md): Prediction markets trade through an order book, the same as any other market on TxFlow.
- [Resolution & Settlement](/prediction/resolution-and-settlement.md): Every market carries predefined rules that determine its final result.

## Product Notices

- [Product Notices](/notices.md): Trading hours, product-specific terms, and risk disclosures for the TxFlow markets that reference off-chain assets.

## Points

## Builder Program

- [Builder Program](/builders.md): Connect your product to every TxFlow market with one integration, and earn trading fees at your own rate on the order flow you route.

- [Instruments](/tip/instrument-config.md): An instrument is a single tradable market — a spot pair, a perpetual contract, or an outcome (prediction) market.

## Appendix: integration rules for coding agents

Hard rules for generating TxFlow client code. Each links the page that states it.

### Endpoints
- Testnet (use it for every example and test): `https://rpc.txflow-testnet.xyz` serves `POST /info`, `POST /exchange`, `wss://…/ws`, `wss://…/api-ws`, and the faucet `POST /request-fund` with `{"address":"0x…"}`. Mainnet: `https://rpc.txflow.com`. TxRelay (`/api/v1/bridge`) is on its own host. — [Networks](/api.md)
- Reads need no auth. There are no API keys: writes are signed locally. — [Builder API Reference](/api.md)
- Send `x-api-version: 2026-08-16` on every `/info` and `/exchange` request; every documented response assumes it. — [Conventions](/api.md)

### Data
- Prices and sizes are strings. They are hashed exactly as written, so `"50000.0"` and `"50000"` sign differently. — [Signing](/api/signing.md)
- An instrument id is the `index` from `perpMeta`, or an Outcome market's `instrument_id` from `outcomeMeta`. In requests, `coin` and the `/info` `asset` filter take it as a numeric **string** (`"coin":"1"`) — every endpoint accepts that, and node reads such as `l2Book` accept nothing else; `instrumentId` / `instrumentIds` and the `/exchange` fields `a` / `asset` take it as an **integer** (`"a":1`). A string `a` changes the MessagePack bytes and breaks the signature. In responses `coin` is a display name whose form varies (`BTC-USDC`, `BTC`, `OUTCOME-4991183`): match rows on `asset` / `instrumentId`, compared as numbers (`asset` is `"1"` in some responses, `1` in others). — [Conventions](/api.md)
- `accountType` is `perp` or `outcome`.
- Private subscriptions and `/info` reads take the **account** address as `user`, never the agent's.
- Outcome metadata responses are snake_case; everything else is camelCase.
- Order prices must be a multiple of `priceTick` and sizes have at most `szDecimals` decimals (both from `perpMeta`). A cloid (`c`) is any string up to 64 bytes; do not start it with `0x` (reserved, rejected with `Invalid cloid format`). — [order](/api/exchange/order.md)
- The Outcome book and balance come from the shared `l2Book` and `clearinghouseState` (`accountType: "outcome"`). — [Info API](/api/info.md)

### Signing
- Two flows. Account key, direct EIP-712: `approveAgent`, `tokenSend`, `withdraw3`, `approveBuilderFee`, `revokeBuilderFee`. Agent key, MessagePack + `Agent` type: `order`, `cancel`, `cancelByCloid`, `modify2`, `outcomeOperate`, `update*`, `claimBuilderRewards`. — [Signing](/api/signing.md)
- EIP-712 domain: `name` `TxFlow-Testnet` / `TxFlow-Mainnet`, `version` `"1"`, `chainId` `2511` / `869`, `verifyingContract` zero address.
- Agent hash: MessagePack the action **without** `type` (exception: `claimBuilderRewards` keeps it) as a map with named keys, append the nonce as 8 bytes big-endian, then the vault flag (`0x00`, or `0x01` + 20 address bytes; `vaultTransfer` always uses `0x00`); `connectionId = keccak256(…)`.
- Keep the node's key order — the key order of each action's request example, which is also the order its `.md` page lists the action fields in; for an order body `a, b, p, s, r, t, c, m, expiresAt`. Never sort keys.
- Omit null optional fields instead of sending `null` (a plain `modify2` has no `tpsl` key). Extra keys break the signature.
- The agent key must be authorized first with `approveAgent`, signed by the account key. The account must be funded first (testnet: the faucet), or it fails with `Please deposit first`. An agent address can be bound to only one account at a time (`Agent address is already used`); revoking frees it. — [approveAgent](/api/exchange/approveAgent.md)
- Signatures must be low-S. `v` is `27`/`28` in JSON. Test vectors are on the Signing page.

### Nonces
- Millisecond timestamp, unique per signer, within 2 days before / 1 day after the block time. Each address keeps its 100 highest nonces. Use a fresh `Date.now()` per request. — [Signing § Nonces](/api/signing.md)
- For direct EIP-712 actions the nonce is also inside `action`; the envelope must repeat the same value.

### Responses
- `/info` returns `{"success":true,"code":0,"data":…}`; on error `success` is `false` with `code` and `message`. Each reference page documents the `data` payload.
- `/exchange` returns `{"status":"ok","code":0,"data":{"type":…,"data":{"statuses":["success"]}}}` — one status for the whole action. `success` means accepted by consensus, not executed; add `"confirm":"executed"` to the request body to wait for execution. The response never reports resting/filled/cancelled or an oid: read those from `orderUpdates` or `frontendOpenOrders`. `data.type` may differ from the request type (`order` → `PlaceOrder`). — [Exchange API § Response](/api/exchange.md)
- A rejection is `{"status":"err","code":<n>,"message":"…"}`; some gateway rejections (rate limits, disabled interfaces) carry the text in `response` instead. Read whichever is present.
- An Outcome order can instead be acknowledged asynchronously as `{"status":"ok","traceId":"…"}` (no `data`), which means queued. With `"confirm":"executed"`, a timeout returns HTTP 202 `{"status":"pending","txHash":"…"}`.
- If a queued Outcome order fails, WebSocket `outcomeOrderUpdate` on `/api-ws` pushes the reason under its `traceId`; successes are not pushed — follow fills on `outcomeOrderUpdates` (`/ws`). Outcome orders accept `Gtc`, `Gtd`, `Alo` only. — [order](/api/exchange/order.md)

### WebSocket
- On `/ws`, every subscribe/unsubscribe frame needs the channel's subscribe type at the **top level** as well as inside `subscription`: `{"method":"subscribe","type":"orderUpdates","subscription":{"type":"orderUpdates","user":"0x…"}}`. Without it the node silently ignores the frame. `/api-ws` takes `subscription` alone. — [WebSocket API](/api/websocket.md)
- Send `{"method":"ping"}` every 10 s on both `/ws` and `/api-ws`; a connection that sends nothing for ~16 s is closed (1006). Pongs are `{"method":"PONG"}` on `/ws` and `{"channel":"pong"}` on `/api-ws` — drop them before dispatching by `channel`. — [WebSocket API](/api/websocket.md)
- On reconnect, re-subscribe every channel; subscriptions do not survive the socket.

### Limits
- Per IP: `/info` 50 req/s, `/exchange` 10 req/s, 10 live connections each on `/ws` and `/api-ws`. Over the limit: HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`; a rate-limited action did not execute, so re-sign it with a fresh nonce. — [Rate limits](/api/rate-limits.md)
- Prefer WebSocket streams to polling, batch orders (≤ 50) and cancels (≤ 200), and cache `perpMeta`.
